guidance.heading: •2026 outlook
section: ◦Comparable EBITDA is revised higher and now expected to be in the range of $11.8 to $12.0 billion3
◦Comparable earnings per common share (EPS) outlook is expected to be higher than 2025, consistent with our 2025 Annual Report

1 Comparable EBITDA, comparable earnings and comparable earnings per common share are non-GAAP measures used throughout this news release. These measures do not have any standardized meaning under GAAP and therefore are unlikely to be comparable to similar measures presented by other companies. The most directly comparable GAAP measures are Segmented earnings, Net income attributable to common shares and Net income per common share, respectively. We do not forecast Segmented earnings. For more information on non-GAAP measures, refer to the Non-GAAP and Supplementary financial measure section of this news release.

2 Build multiple is a non-GAAP ratio calculated by dividing capital expenditures by comparable EBITDA. Weighted average build multiple is calculated across all projects based on each project's capital expenditures. Please note our method for calculating build multiple may differ from methods used by other entities. Therefore, it may not be comparable to similar measures presented by other entities. For more information on non-GAAP measures and the supplementary financial measure, refer to the Non-GAAP and Supplementary financial measure section of this news release.
3 Based on forecasted 2026 annual average USD/CAD foreign exchange rate of 1.38.
◦Capital expenditures are anticipated to be at the lower end of $6.0 to $6.5 billion prior to adjustments for non-controlling interests, or $5.5 to $6.0 billion of net capital expenditures1

desk.headline: Comparable EPS up 22% to C$0.94, beat; 2026 EBITDA outlook raised to C$11.8–12.0bn and new 2027 range given

numbers.eps_basis: adjusted (comparable EPS); estimate is the LSEG average in C$

results: Comparable EBITDA rose 13% to C$3.0bn and comparable EPS climbed to C$0.94 from C$0.77; GAAP EPS was C$0.98.
U.S. gas pipelines led, with EBITDA up 17% to C$1.2bn, helped by rate settlements and storage revenue; Power and Energy Solutions EBITDA rose 35% to C$360m.
Gas volumes grew in all three countries: Canadian deliveries up 6%, U.S. flows up 3% and Mexico flows up 8%; Bruce Power ran at 96.6% availability.
About C$3bn of new projects were approved, including the US$1.8bn Crossroads Expansion and Coastal GasLink Phase 2, taking 2026 approvals to about C$6bn.
The quarterly dividend was kept at C$0.8775 (C$3.51 a year).

guidance.summary: TC Energy lifted its 2026 comparable EBITDA outlook, gave a first 2027 range slightly above the analyst average, and now targets 5–7% yearly EBITDA growth to 2031. It still expects 2026 comparable EPS above 2025.

points: Management credited the 2026 upgrade to high asset availability, U.S. rate settlements, extra storage revenue and projects finishing early and under budget.
Projects placed in service since 2025 came in more than 10% under budget overall; about C$3.4bn should be in service in 2026.
It expects North American gas demand to grow about 51 Bcf/d from 2025 to 2035, led by LNG exports and gas-fired power, including data centres.
The five-year outlook rests on nearly C$25bn of approved projects, about C$6bn awaiting approval and over C$40bn more in development.
Debt-to-EBITDA is to stay below the 4.75 times long-term target, with about 98% of EBITDA from regulated or contracted assets.
call.source: CEO message in the news release (Exhibit 99.1); no independent call coverage found. Consensus from Reuters via BNN Bloomberg, 5 Nov 2026

watch: Whether more of the C$6bn of pending projects is approved, and at what build multiple.
FERC approval of the GTN rate settlement and the second Coastal GasLink First Nations deal due in Q4.
Progress on Bruce Power's Unit 4 and Unit 5 refurbishments.

sources.title: TC Energy raises 2026 profit outlook, announces $3B in pipeline projects — BNN Bloomberg (Reuters), 5 Nov 2026
